Nebius Group (NBIS): Expectations for Q2 Results

prediction_based_investment_rating.most_reasonable_investment_thesis_scenar:
The operating argument is already won; the equity now trades on the financing argument. Nebius has secured the scarce inputs — power, shells and next-generation Nvidia allocation — and repriced capacity from roughly $12M to $20-25M ACV per megawatt [3][4], with more than $40B of contracted revenue from investment-grade counterparties behind it [13]. The base case is that guidance is broadly met, revenue scales toward double-digit billions, and the AI cloud segment sustains high adjusted margins. But capital consumption of $20-25B annually [4] means shareholders fund that growth through in-the-money converts and share sales, so enterprise value compounds faster than value per share.
- FY2026 guidance implies $3-3.4B revenue and $7-9B exit ARR; $62.7B equals roughly 7-9x forward ARR.
- Per-share outcome hinges on dilution: converts striking near $183 plus warrants expand the 280M share base materially.
- Cross-check: 5GW contracted at $20M ACV per megawatt implies capital needs vastly exceeding current cash generation.
prediction_based_investment_rating.bull_case_scenario: The bull case activates when the financing constraint dissolves. If 2027 guidance lands above $20M per megawatt across more than 1GW and the July 2026 secured template [19] is repeated at scale, dilution stops, the cost of capital falls, and each incremental megawatt becomes accretive rather than dilutive. That loop is reflexive: cheaper capital buys more power, more contracted power justifies cheaper capital. Shareholders would then own a digital-infrastructure compounder at an infrastructure multiple, not a speculative neocloud.
prediction_based_investment_rating.bear_case_scenario: The bear case activates when connection schedules slip while capex is already committed. A Vineland-style delay [26] or grid bottleneck misses the H2 2026 revenue step-change of roughly $2.2B [21], the convert window prices punitively, and Nebius issues equity into weakness with $13.5B of debt against $1.36B of TTM revenue [9]. Hyperscaler digestion then depresses renewal pricing, Meta's backstop fills clusters at contract rather than market rates [11], and depreciation swamps adjusted EBITDA. Permanent per-share impairment follows.
prediction_based_investment_rating.thesis_watchpoints:
- Confirms: Q3 and Q4 2026 prints delivering 800MW-1GW connected and ARR tracking the $7-9B exit band.
- Weakens: another multi-billion convertible before mid-2027 at coupons above 4.5%, signalling closed secured-debt capacity.
- Reassess: renewal pricing on 2026-vintage clusters printing below $15M ACV per megawatt at any point from 2028.

broader_narrative_signals.today_crowd_consensus_narrative: The crowd treats the operating argument as settled: power is scarce, Nebius has 5GW contracted and pricing doubled to $20-25M per megawatt, so backlog equals destiny. Shares nearly tripled year-to-date [7], and 46x TTM sales anchors on forward ARR rather than earnings. Sell-side dispersion of $120-$415 [23] reveals the real disagreement: nobody agrees on the discount rate or the share count.
broader_narrative_signals.alpha_gap_assessment: The crowd overestimates what today's shareholders capture, even while correctly valuing the enterprise. Two pieces of evidence are under-modelled: March 2026 converts strike near $183 and are already in the money [17], and H1 financing of $9.16B included $2.85B of treasury-share sales plus $2.0B of prefunded warrants [16]. Enterprise value can compound handsomely while per-share value stalls. Add adjusted EBITDA excluding $260M of quarterly depreciation [21], and the equity is priced for flawless capacity delivery at flat funding costs.
broader_narrative_signals.the_convergence_catalyst: Formal 2027 guidance, expected in the Q4 2026 or Q1 2027 print [1], forces disclosure of capex, funding plan and fully diluted share count together. The first observable repricing sign is whether that guidance is accompanied by secured, non-dilutive financing rather than another convertible tranche.
broader_narrative_signals.macro_regime_alignment: The macro wind is in its face through the funding channel. With the Fed at 3.75-4.00% and the 10-year near 4.998%, a company financing decade-long assets with seven-year paper saw coupons jump from 1.25% to 4.50% in five months [17][18]. Demand remains rate-insensitive; the balance sheet is not.

financial_review_fields.earnings_and_financials_trend_assessment:
The revenue story is extraordinary and the earnings story is an illusion. Q2 2026 group revenue reached $582M, up 454% year-on-year, with AI cloud at 98% of the total and ARR of $3.0B at June-end [1][2]. Yet TTM operating income is minus $669M while TTM net income shows plus $61.6M, because H1 profit sits entirely in Q1's non-operating $621M gain [1].

What the headline conceals matters more than what it reveals. Depreciation is now $260M per quarter and rising with the fleet [21], so GAAP results will deteriorate before they improve. Recurring performance must be judged on segment adjusted EBITDA near 50% and contracted ACV per megawatt, not reported net income.
financial_review_fields.capex_and_investment_intensity_trend_ass:
This is one of the most capital-intensive growth stories in public markets. Q2 2026 capex was $5.66B and H1 $8.13B, lifting property and equipment to $13.05B from $5.55B at year-end 2025 [15]; FY2026 guidance is $20-25B [4]. TTM free cash flow of minus $3.65B understates the run-rate drain already visible in the second-quarter figures.

Management's priority is unambiguous: land-grab the power queue before rivals, funded by anything available. The mitigating evidence is contractual, not financial — upfront customer payments cover 50-60% of associated capex [4], and the secured facility plus customer cash flows cover more than 100% of one deployment's capex [19]. Payback therefore hinges on renewal pricing after three-year GPU lives.
financial_review_fields.balance_sheet_strength_and_leverage_asse:
Headline liquidity looks comfortable and is deceptive. Cash stood at $8.04B on 30 June 2026 against non-current debt of $8.50B [15], but the August 2026 offering added $5.75B of converts plus $800M exchanged for shares [18], and third-party analysis puts total debt near $13.5B against $1.36B of TTM revenue [9].

The concealed commitment is capex, not debt: $20-25B of guided annual spending is a contractual obligation to suppliers and customers alike. Resilience rests on prepayments, the Meta backstop [11] and Nvidia's equity participation [14]; vulnerability rests on rollover. No credit rating has been awarded — Nebius sells to investment-grade counterparties, it is not one.
financial_review_fields.profitability_margins_trend_assessment:
Margins are improving structurally and the reported picture flatters them. Gross margin reached 68.6% in FY2025 from 37.5% in FY2024, and the AI cloud segment now runs near 50% adjusted EBITDA on dedicated, multi-year contracts [2][9]. The cause is genuine operating leverage: fixed shells and power contracts spread over rapidly rising revenue per connected megawatt.

The divergence is the tell. FY2025 operating margin was minus 113% and the TTM figure remains deeply negative, because adjusted metrics exclude roughly $260M of quarterly depreciation and $103M of stock-based compensation [21]. Repricing legacy $12M-per-megawatt contracts toward $20M-plus [3] is the structural improvement; everything else is timing.

drivers.event_name: Power scarcity rent, not GPU scarcity
drivers.description: Follow the pricing evidence: Q2 2026 deals cleared at $20-25M annual contract value per megawatt against a 2026 installed base priced near $12M, with short-dated Q3 capacity above $40M [3][4]. A maiden auction cleared 15% above prior Blackwell highs, and on-demand list prices rise from 1 October 2026 [1][6]. Interconnects and shells, not silicon, bind supply; that rent persists while power queues stay congested.

Nebius states more than $40 billion of contracted revenue from investment-grade counterparties including Microsoft and Meta [13]. The March 2026 Meta agreement supplies $12 billion of five-year dedicated Vera Rubin capacity, total contract value up to roughly $27 billion, and obliges Meta to buy clusters Nebius fails to sell elsewhere [10][11]. That order book converts speculative capex into financeable, visible cash flow, which is precisely what lenders price.

The AI cloud segment delivered roughly 50% adjusted EBITDA margin in Q2 2026 on $575M of segment revenue [2][9], while new contracts carry upfront payments covering 50-60% of associated capex [4]. That structure shortens the working-capital cycle and reduces reliance on the capital markets at the margin. Operating leverage per connected megawatt should persist while utilization stays near sold-out and contracts remain dedicated rather than spot.

drivers.event_name: From equity dilution to secured paper
drivers.description: The July 2026 $775M senior secured facility, backed by deployed GPU infrastructure and an investment-grade customer's contracted cash flows at SOFR plus 250bps to October 2030, covers more than 100% of the underlying deployment's capex [19]. Repeating that structure migrates funding from dilutive converts toward asset-level debt. Nvidia's $2 billion investment reinforces allocation priority for scarce next-generation silicon [14], lowering both capital and supply risk.

frictions.description: Follow the share count, not the revenue. H1 2026 financing inflows reached $9,160.4M, comprising $4,337.5M of converts, $2,846.7M of treasury-share sales and $2,000.0M of prefunded warrants [16]. March 2026 notes convert near $183 and $180, deep in the money at $224 [17]; August added $5.75B plus 15.8 million exchange shares [18]. Enterprise growth is real, but per-share economics leak continuously while capex runs at $20-25B annually [4].

Same issuer, five months apart: 1.25% on March 2031 notes versus 4.50% on the August 2034 tranche [17][18]. That is the convert market repricing duration risk on neoclouds while the Fed sits at 3.75-4.00% and the US 10-year closed near 4.998% on 18 September 2026. For a business financing multi-decade assets with seven-year paper, every 100bps raises the hurdle rate and compresses the multiple investors will pay.

The headline 41% group adjusted EBITDA margin excludes roughly $260M of hardware depreciation and $103M of stock-based compensation in the quarter [21]. TTM operating income is minus $669M against TTM net income of plus $61.6M, and H1 profitability sits entirely in Q1's non-operating $621M gain [1]. Depreciation is the true cost of a GPU fleet; as the installed base ages, GAAP results will converge downward on economics.

Concentration cuts both ways. Meta explicitly declined to guide 2027 capex [9], and the unsold-capacity backstop converts Nebius from price-setter to price-taker on that tranche if third-party demand softens [11]. A hyperscaler digestion phase would arrive while $20B-plus of annual capex is already committed, squeezing renewal pricing on 2026-vintage clusters and the spread per megawatt that underwrites the entire valuation.

tail_opportunities.description: The decisive catalyst would be a first credit rating plus repeatable asset-level securitization, plausibly during 2027-2028, extending the July 2026 secured template across the fleet [19]. Nebius would then fund 1GW-plus annual builds with amortizing secured debt at low-single-digit spreads instead of equity-linked paper, halting dilution and re-rating the equity from speculative growth toward digital infrastructure. It stays below 50% because rating agencies dislike single-asset-class collateral with three-year technology obsolescence and two dominant counterparties.

Formal 2027 guidance, promised later in 2026 [1], could be issued at greater than $20M ACV per megawatt across more than 1GW of new capacity, implying 2027 revenue well beyond current sell-side modelling. Management already claims it could sell all 2027 capacity today on those terms [4]. Delivered in the Q4 2026 or Q1 2027 print, that would reset forward ARR multiples sharply higher. It stays below 50% because the Vineland schedule and grid connections remain unproven at this scale [26].

tail_risks.event_name: AI capex digestion cracks renewal pricing
tail_risks.description: Should hyperscalers pause incremental orders in 2028-2029 after three years of frantic build, 2026-vintage clusters would renew far below $20M per megawatt, Meta's backstop would fill capacity at contract rather than market prices [11], and depreciation would overwhelm adjusted EBITDA. With roughly $13.5B of debt against $1.36B of TTM revenue [9], deleveraging would require equity issuance into weakness. It remains below 50% because inference demand and power scarcity both argue for extended tightness.

The binary is timing. Guidance requires roughly $2.2B of H2 2026 revenue after $981M in H1 and ARR moving from $3.0B to $7-9B in six months [21]. A Vineland-style slippage or grid delay that pushes connected megawatts below the 800MW-1GW plan [8][26] would miss revenue while $20B-plus of capex is already committed, and the convert market would demand punitive terms precisely when funding is needed. Probability stays under 50% because capacity is substitutable across sites and prepayments cushion cash.

timeseries.scenario_rationale: November's Q3 print should show the guided step-change beginning, with connected megawatts moving toward 800MW-1GW and October on-demand price increases landing. Treasury yields near 5% cap multiple expansion, so operating delivery carries the quarter.

Formal 2027 guidance arrives alongside FY2026 results, with exit ARR near the $7-9B band and Meta's Vera Rubin deliveries commencing. Forward ARR multiples expand despite another expected financing announcement diluting holders.

Financing gravity reasserts itself. A further multi-billion raise, share settlement of in-the-money March 2026 converts and stepping depreciation compress per-share economics while policy rates remain restrictive and long yields elevated.

Mid-2027 results demonstrate repricing flowing into revenue as legacy $12M-per-megawatt contracts roll onto $20M-plus terms. Segment adjusted EBITDA holds near fifty percent, restoring momentum and narrowing the sell-side dispersion.

Hyperscaler 2028 capex signalling dominates the tape. Contracted backlog cushions sentiment, but investors begin explicitly discounting GPU obsolescence cycles and the cash cost of another gigawatt build, limiting upside.

A digestion scare hits the cohort: slower incremental orders and a widening gap between adjusted EBITDA and GAAP losses compress multiples. Nebius trades on its funding schedule rather than its growth rate.

Repeatable asset-level securitization and progress toward a first credit rating lower marginal funding costs. Contracted cash flows from investment-grade counterparties reassure holders, lifting the equity off oversold levels.

Revenue scale approaches double-digit billions with the AI cloud segment generating positive operating income. Capacity sold before commissioning sustains a modest advance against still-elevated real yields and heavier interest expense.

The cycle's first genuine air pocket. Renewal pricing on 2026-vintage clusters disappoints, Meta's backstop converts Nebius into a price-taker on unsold capacity, and credit markets demand materially higher coupons.
Refinancing of 2029-2030 maturities coincides with softer spot GPU pricing. Impairment of older Blackwell fleets and slower connection additions keep valuation pressure on a leveraged balance sheet.

Stabilization phase: capex intensity moderates as the build completes, the free cash flow deficit narrows sharply, and investors recalibrate onto cash generation per connected megawatt rather than backlog headlines.

Inference rather than training drives utilization, extending the useful economic life of installed accelerators. Improving cash conversion supports a firmer, less narrative-dependent valuation and reduces equity issuance need.
Expectations of easier policy and lower long yields aid long-duration infrastructure equities. A maturing contract book and minimal dilution permit modest multiple recovery into year-end positioning.

Full-year 2029 results show sustained positive operating income and largely self-funded expansion. Sovereign and enterprise contracts dilute two-counterparty dependence, allowing valuation on earnings rather than annualized run-rate revenue.

Competitive supply catches up as power interconnection queues clear and hyperscalers insource capacity. Per-megawatt pricing normalizes toward the mid-teens, trimming the spread that justified premium multiples.

Scale asserts itself in a consolidating neocloud market. Nebius absorbs distressed capacity cheaply, and industry consolidation improves pricing discipline and returns on invested capital for surviving operators.

Trailing free cash flow turns positive as depreciation finally trails revenue. Debt reduction or buybacks, rather than dilution, become the marginal capital-allocation decision, benefiting per-share economics.

A mature infrastructure framework applies: enterprise value per contracted megawatt and free cash flow yield replace revenue multiples, delivering steady rather than spectacular appreciation on delivered earnings.

Growth decelerates toward low double digits with defensible margins. The equity behaves like a leveraged digital-infrastructure operator, tracking credit spreads and power-cost inflation more than AI headlines.

Horizon close: contracted renewals at stable pricing, moderate leverage and disciplined capex sustain compounding. The residual claim finally reflects cash earnings rather than promised capacity and adjusted metrics.
